html:
The Monqui were a people of the Gulf coast of Baja California Sur, Mexico, around Loreto, holding some 65 kilometres of coast. They spoke a Guaycuran language, related to that of the Guaycura to the south, while the Cochimí lived inland and to the north.

They lived by fishing, gathering shellfish and desert plants, and hunting. In 1697 the Jesuit Juan María de Salvatierra founded the mission of Loreto in their land, the first lasting Spanish settlement in the Californias and for a long time its capital. Epidemics followed, and within a century the Monqui had died out or merged into the mission population.
